subject: Next steps: PR intake + supplier ID options for Acme Retail
messages:
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>

Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-12-01T15:10:00Z
Subject: Post-call recap + procurement path questions

Hi Susan — thanks for the intro call today. Quick recap and two asks so we can line up procurement on our side: 

Call recap (2 min):
- You’re evaluating Redwood for product search relevance and chat assist across 3 internal apps; pilot scope ~3 months, ~100k tokens/day expected at peak.
- Primary procurement route: likely standard PO via Coupa, but you’re checking whether marketplace (AWS Marketplace) or card payment would be acceptable for a short-term POC.
- Team: you (procurement lead), Finance Ops (cc’d), and an internal IT security reviewer to follow up on SOC2 questions.

Asks / next steps:
1) Can you confirm which path looks most likely: PO (Coupa/Ariba) vs corporate card vs marketplace? If PO, does your supplier onboarding require a vendor ID up front?
2) If PO, what’s the internal target timeline for raising a PR (purchase requisition)? Example: today → PR raised in 1–2 weeks → PO issued in 3–4 weeks.

I attached a short proposal draft for the pilot (proposal-draft.pdf). If it helps, Marissa can send a one-page supplier onboarding checklist we usually share with procurement teams.

Thanks — I’ll hold availability tomorrow 9–11am PT if you want an internal follow-up with Finance Ops.

Best,
Marcus
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marcus.lin@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0192

From: Susan Kelly <susan.kelly@acme-retail.com>

Cc: Finance Ops <finance_ops@acme-retail.com>
Date: 2026-12-02T09:05:00Z
Subject: Re: Post-call recap + procurement path questions

Marcus — thanks for the clear recap. Short answers below: 

1) Procurement direction: PO via Coupa is the expected path for any contracted vendor. Marketplace only considered if there’s a clear short-term billing advantage and legal signs off; card payment is possible but needs Finance approval and usually only for low-dollar pilots.

2) PR timeline: our typical cadence is 
   - Request/Business justification submitted (PR creation) — 2–5 business days once we have required vendor docs
   - Supplier creation (if new) can add 5–10 business days depending on tax forms and W-9 processing

Supplier creation: we will need the vendor’s legal name, tax ID (EIN), remit address, W-9, and a primary AP contact. Also let us know whether Redwood is already in Coupa with a supplier ID — that speeds things up.

I’ll loop in Finance Ops for anything specific on payment terms.

Susan
Susan Kelly
Senior Procurement Manager — Acme Retail
susan.kelly@acme-retail.com

Subject: Supplier/PR intake checklist + Coupa steps (pilot-friendly)

Hi Susan — following up with a concrete checklist and guidance your team can drop into the PR ticket. I’m including both Coupa and an Ariba note in case your procurement team prefers one over the other. Attached: redwood-coupa-supplier-steps.pdf and pr-template.xlsx.

High-level supplier info we need to provision a supplier record in Coupa/Ariba (minimal required set):
- Legal business name (as on W-9)
- Tax ID / EIN
- Remit address (for invoices)
- W-9 (signed PDF) or equivalent tax form for your region
- Primary AP contact (name, email, phone)
- Preferred payment terms (Net 30 default; specify if you need Net 45/60)

Suggested PR ticket body (copy/paste into ServiceNow or internal PR intake):
- Business owner: [name]
- Redwood Inference (supplier) details: legal name, EIN, remit address, W-9 attached, primary AP contact
- Pilot scope: 3-month pilot, up to 100k tokens/day, estimated spend $X/month
- Contract pointer: HubSpot deal ACME-EXP-2026-0911 (link below)

Coupa-specific notes: 
- If Redwood already has a supplier ID in Coupa, provide the 6-digit supplier ID in the PR — procurement will link to the existing vendor and skip creation steps.
- If new, our vendor onboarding pack (W-9, bank details only at PO stage) will be sufficient to create the supplier record. Typical internal SLA ~7 business days.

Ariba alternative:
- Ariba tends to require the same minimal docs, but onboarding is routed through a different intake team; let me know if you want our Ariba contact (we’ll share a short form).

Faster option (pilot kick-off):
- If Acme can approve payment by corporate card for month 1, we can start engineering work immediately and convert to PO once the supplier ID is live — many customers use this route to avoid a 2–3 week wait.

I’ve attached simplified step-by-step PDF (redwood-coupa-supplier-steps.pdf) and a PR template you can paste into ServiceNow (pr-template.xlsx).

Let me know if you want me to open a short vendor packet for your team or if you want me to walk through the ServiceNow fields with an AP analyst.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com
